title: The warehouse that answered too much
scenario: A parts supplier gives its sales team a chat assistant with two tools: `find_stock` (looks up parts in the warehouse database) and `send_quote_email` (emails a price quote). Sales reps report three problems: answers about stock are slow and sometimes miss the part they asked for, the whole chat crashes when the supplier API is down, and after sending a quote the assistant says it is not sure the email went out. You pull one trace (exhibit).
exhibit:
CALL  find_stock(query="M8 hex bolt")
RESULT (2,812 rows, 41 columns each)
  row_uuid=9f3c.., sku_internal=0x00A3.., bin=..., created_at=..., ...
  ...

CALL  find_stock(query="M8 hex bolt", warehouse="north")
RESULT  <Python traceback: TimeoutError at supplier_api.py line 88>
  -> chat session crashed, user saw "Something went wrong"

CALL  send_quote_email(customer="Kade Ltd", quote_id="Q-5531")
RESULT  (empty)
ASSISTANT  I tried to send the quote, but I'm not sure it went through.

questions.prompt: What is the best fix for the first `find_stock` result?

options.text: Return only the needed fields, cap the rows, and add filter or page parameters.
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs say to return only high-signal information, and Anthropic's tool guide suggests pagination, filtering or truncation with sensible defaults.

options.text: Keep the full result, but move to a model with a bigger context window so all the rows fit.
options.explanation: A bigger window fits more noise, but the Claude docs warn that bloated responses waste context. The fix is a smaller, focused result.

options.text: Return the rows as one compressed string with no column names.
options.explanation: Shorter but harder to read. The model would have to guess which value is the stock level.

options.text: Ask the user to type the exact internal SKU so the result has one row.
options.explanation: That moves the tool's job onto the user. The tool should do the filtering and return what matters.

questions.prompt: The supplier API timed out and the whole chat crashed. What should the code do instead?

options.text: Retry the API call in a loop until the supplier answers, however long that takes.
options.explanation: An unbounded retry can hang the chat. The model should hear about the failure so it can tell the user or try something else.

options.text: Return an empty result, so the model thinks there is simply no stock.
options.explanation: That turns an outage into a false answer: the rep would hear the part is out of stock.

options.text: Catch it and return it as an error result (on Claude, `is_error: true`).
options.explanation: Right. The Claude tutorial says to send the error back instead of crashing; the model can retry, ask the user, or explain the limitation.

options.text: Remove the `warehouse` parameter, since the call that used it failed.
options.explanation: The parameter did not cause a timeout. The supplier API was down, which can happen on any call.

questions.prompt: Which error text should the tool return for the timeout?

options.explanation: An opaque code. Anthropic's tool guide says to give specific, actionable messages rather than opaque error codes.

options.text: "Supplier API timed out. Stock is unknown right now. Tell the user and suggest retrying in a few minutes."
options.explanation: Right. It says what went wrong and what to do next, as the Claude docs advise.

options.text: The full Python traceback with file names and line numbers, so the model has every detail it might need.
options.explanation: Anthropic's tool guide names tracebacks as what to avoid. They cost tokens and say nothing about the next step.
The Claude docs use "failed" as the example of a generic error to avoid.

questions.prompt: After `send_quote_email`, the assistant is not sure the email was sent. What fixes this?

options.text: Tell the model in the system prompt to always say the email was sent.
options.explanation: That makes it claim success even when sending fails. The result should report what actually happened.

options.text: Remove the tool result, since the email tool has nothing to return.
options.explanation: Every call needs a result. On Claude, a call without a matching `tool_result` returns an error.

options.text: Make the model call `send_quote_email` twice, to be safe.
options.explanation: That can send the customer two emails. The real gap is that the result says nothing.

options.text: Return a short status string, such as "sent to orders@kade.example, quote Q-5531" or the failure reason.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says a function with no return value should return a string that indicates success or failure.
